newsitem.title: USA: Ballot questions and bond referendums by state.
newsitem.headline: Ballot questions and bond referendums by state.

text.p: The following is a list of upcoming ballot initiatives and measures affecting municipal finance.
P - passed. D - defeated. NA - not available.
--Two tax ballot issues to raise $60 million in Los Angeles County.
P --Broward County community of Bonaventure vote on whether to join City of Sunrise or City of Weston. (Voters chose Weston).
--Marion County, half-cent sales tax increase for schools.
--Oglethorpe County, five-year extension of special purpose one-cent sales tax increase.
--Up to $800 million of Broward County general obligation bonds for schools.
--Vote in Adams (D), McDonough (P), McLean (D), Shelby (D) and Stephenson (P) counties on property tax and general obligation bond limitations on local governments.
--Cherry Hill, N.J., votes on $97.5 million school budget, including a tax increase of 5.5 cents per $100 of assessed value.
--New Milford, N.J., votes on $16.7 million school budget, including a property tax increase of six cents per $100 of assessed value.

--Northern Highlands Regional High School District, N.J., votes on three separate ballot questions: a $1.62 million bond issue for computers and technology improvements; a $395,600 bond for an all-weather track and auditorium upgrades; and a $636,600 bond for gym improvements and other upgrades.
--Perth Amboy, N.J., voters decide whether to raise taxes to support an $81.1 million school budget.
--Vorhees, N.J., votes decide whether to approve a $30.6 million Board of Education budget that would raise the school tax rated 15.5 cents per $100 of assessed value.

--Woodbury, N.J., voters decide two questions: whether to raise taxes by $6.4 million to support the regular budget for fiscal 1998, and whether to raise taxes an additional $208,391 to maintain moderate class sizes and five elementary school teaching positions.
--$6.6 million Caldwell School District, N.J., school general obligation bonds, for school renovations and technology improvements.
--Wood-Ridge and Hasbrouck Heights, N.J., vote on forming a new regional school district.
--$71.5 million City of High Point GO bonds for streets and recreation.
--$4.5 million Hoke County water system bonds.
--$59.5 million Dare County GO bonds for schools.
--Franklin County vote on 0.5 percent sales tax for sports complex.
--$61 million Lexington County School District 1, GO bonds for schools.
P --$31 million GO bonds for Sioux Falls school district.
--$73.3 million Loudoun County school bond issue for school contruction and renovations.
